items.title: Burrill Crohn interviewed by Monk Rowe, Woodstock, New York, January 3, 2012
items.q: I don’t think I’ve had the sort of like blessed life Warren had, where he started listening to music under the piano hearing Rubenstein playing.

ctx.x: Did you ever have moments where you are saying why am I doing this?

Oh yeah, of course. Of course. If I knew how to do anything else I’d probably be doing something else. I mean raising money, I’m getting older and running on location and doing this and producing this and worrying and this and that. But no, Warren talks about feeling blessed. I don’t think I’ve had the sort of like blessed life Warren had, where he started listening to music under the piano hearing Rubenstein playing. But I feel blessed that I’ve been able to — every film that I’ve done that’s been any good,…

on television, has been about music. And there is something about — I don’t think I’m a great filmmaker at all. I mean there are people with way better technical chops than me. But if I love it, it seems to come out better. If I don’t love it, it doesn’t come out good at all. So I’m not good at doing commercials or doing industrial films, because if I don’t love it, there are twenty people that do it better than me — a hundred and twenty people — twelve hundred people.
